newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour Party backs referendum on voting reform.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour Party backs referendum on voting reform.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour and Liberal Democrat parties said on Wednesday they had reached agreement on plans for reforming the constitution, including holding a referendum on whether to adopt proportional representation (PR).
Labour's Foreign Affairs spokesman Robin Cook said agreement had been reached with the minority Liberal Democrats, long supporters of PR, to put the issue to the British people.
Labour are opinion poll favourites to win the next general election, expected to be held on May 1, which will use Britain's traditional "first past the post" system.
Cook and Robert MacLennnan of the Liberal Democrats will publish a joint report on constitutional reform later on Wednesday.

It is expected to cover reform of the unelected upper House of Lords, removing the vote from hereditary peers, and devolution for Scotland and Wales, and to recommend that a commission be set up to decide on the best form of proportional representation for voting for the British parliament.
Cook said Labour wanted to let the British people decide through a referendum between the present voting system and PR, but the party would not make a recommendation.
"We think it's time power was returned to the people," Cook said on BBC radio.

"I am well known for supporting the case for change in the system but as a party we are not putting forward a view in favour of change. What we are saying is that it is time the question was put to the people."

The fact that the ruling Conservative Party has at general elections managed to win a majority in parliament while not winning a majority of the popular vote has always irritated the Liberal Democrats, who have fared badly under the present voting system.

"I'm extremely happy that there is now a real prospect that early in the life of the next government the decision will be taken by the British people whether or not to dispose of the old system of election which has produced distorted results and government by minority for a very long time," Maclennan said.
"The government of the day today has never had a majority in 18 years, yet it has behaved as though it had the power to do anything it liked," he added.
